Let \(AB=x\), so \(AD=x+9\). Since \(CD=AB=x\) and \(E\) lies on \(CD\), let \(DE=y\), so \(EC=x-y\).

Area condition:
\[
\frac{AB+EC}{2}\cdot AD = 5\cdot \frac12 DE\cdot AD
\]
\[
\frac{x+(x-y)}{2}(x+9)=5\cdot \frac12 y(x+9)
\]
Canceling \(\frac{x+9}{2}\):
\[
2x-y=5y \implies y=\frac{x}{3}.
\]

Perimeter condition:
\[
P_{\text{trap}}-P_{\text{tri}}=68
\]
The shared side \(AE\) cancels:
\[
(AB+BC+CE)-(AD+DE)=68
\]
\[
\left(x+(x+9)+(x-y)\right)-\left((x+9)+y\right)=68
\]
\[
2x-2y=68
\]
Using \(y=\frac{x}{3}\):
\[
2x-\frac{2x}{3}=68 \implies \frac{4x}{3}=68 \implies x=51.
\]
Thus \(AD=60\), so
\[
[ABCD]=51\cdot 60=3060.
\]

\[
\boxed{3060}
\]
